memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and a basket of bread made with the finest flour and without yeast—thick loaves with olive oil mixed in, and thin loaves brushed with olive oil. The priest is to present all these before the Lord and make the sin offering and the burnt offering. He is to present the basket of unleavened bread and is to sacrifice the ram as a fellowship offering to the Lord, together with its grain offering and drink offering.' - Num 6:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The completion of the vow involved a generous array of offerings — lambs, a ram, grain, drink, and a basket of fine bread made with the best flour and oil. This was not a small or stingy gift. It was abundant, and it reflected a heart glad to give lavishly to God.

There is something beautiful about the generosity here. The Nazirite, at the end of a long devotion, did not bring the cheapest, smallest offering they could get away with. They brought the finest flour, rich loaves, good oil. Their giving matched the gladness of their hearts.

This challenges us gently. How do we give to God — our time, our money, our energy, our worship? Do we give Him our leftovers and scraps, or do we bring Him our best? God is not impressed by the size of the gift for its own sake, but He does look at the heart behind it. He loves a cheerful, generous giver (2 Cor 9:7).

We must be careful here not to hear a prosperity message. This abundance flowed from a heart devoted to God; it was not a scheme to get blessings from Him. The generosity was the fruit of love, not a transaction for reward.

When our hearts are full of gratitude for who God is and what He has done in Christ, giving Him our best becomes a joy, not a burden. Bring God your finest today — your best attention, your fullest worship, your generous love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you give God your best, or only your leftovers?
- Does your giving flow from gratitude and love?
- What "finest flour" can you bring to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have given me Your very best in Christ. Teach me to bring You my finest — my best worship, love, and service — with a glad and grateful heart. Amen.
